chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Harun ibn Mufaffaq al-Madaini, from his father, who said:

The late one (peace be upon him) sent for me one day, so I ate in his presence, and there was much sweet dish (halwa). So I said, 'How abundant is this sweet dish!' He (peace be upon him) said: 'We and our Shias were created from sweetness, so we love the sweet dish.'

key_terms.الْمَاضِي: The late one (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Why do the Imams and their Shias love sweets according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Imam (peace be upon him) employs a linguistic and spiritual metaphor, linking the physical sweetness of confectionery (halwa) to the inner purity and gentleness of the Ahl al-Bayt and their Shias, who are described as being created from 'al-halawah' (sweetness). This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of finding deep spiritual realities in everyday customs, suggesting that the affection for sweets is not merely a gustatory preference but a reflection of the innate sweetness of the faithful's souls. It underscores the concept of 'wilayah' as a source of spiritual delight and ease for the believers.
